title: How Submarine Crews Eat, Shower and Sleep for 90 Days

scenes.say: You're about to spend ninety days inside a steel tube. No windows. No sunlight. And no way to call home.
Around one hundred and fifty sailors share a hull about as long as one and a half football fields.
Problem one: sleep. Your bed is a narrow shelf, stacked three high, with barely enough room to roll over. On some boats, junior sailors share one bunk in shifts. It's called hot racking.
Problem two: water. Every drop is made from seawater, so you take a Navy shower. Water on. Water off. Soap. Water on. Done in two minutes.
Problem three: food. Fresh fruit and milk run out in about two weeks. After that, it's frozen, canned, and powdered, for the next eleven weeks.
But the hardest part isn't any of that. It's the air. Because down here, you have to make your own.
